Network

Operations and release runbooks

A maintainable first deployment is two zone processes, one backend and one database—not an unmeasured global MMO platform.

On this page
Boot and readinessDrain/restartBackup restorePatch/security incidentCapacity reporting

Boot and readiness

Start the database and authenticated backend, check migration/catalog compatibility, then start zone processes and register capacity. Admit only after world definitions/spawns/service adapter are ready. Frontend shows maintenance rather than creating a local fallback character when infrastructure is unavailable.

Drain/restart

  1. Announce maintenance with localized UI and operational deadline. Stop new instance reservations/admissions to draining zones.
  2. Freeze new economic starts, cancel unresolved gathers/fishing by policy and wait for accepted command receipts; inspect stuck transactions.
  3. Persist/fence current session snapshots and route players to compatible zones or controlled reconnect.
  4. Stop process, deploy tested build/catalog, restart and validate readiness before reopening admissions.
  5. Confirm no stale epoch writes, duplicate grants or leaked capacity reservations. Preserve redacted incident evidence.

Backup restore

Automated backup success is not restore proof. Restore to an isolated environment, apply supported migrations, validate item uniqueness/occupancy, currency ledgers, reward claims and session/ticket invalidation. Record RecoveryPoint/RecoveryTime objectives as proposals until measured; communicate any acknowledged-operation loss under the actual disaster policy rather than silently replaying client data.

Patch/security incident

Quarantine incompatible builds, stop admissions to compromised processes, rotate service credentials, revoke relevant sessions, inspect immutable economic receipts and apply audited corrections only. Keep administrative capabilities separate from zone/client capabilities. A source-control rollback is not automatically a safe database rollback.

Capacity reporting

Publish the tested zone population, encounter/node/projectile count, hardware, build and duration. Compare generic replication to one selected alternative in a controlled branch. Iris and Replication Graph cannot be configured together. Do not turn a small-session success into a promise of thousands of concurrent players.

Evidence and external references

External links need internet; the manual itself remains offline. Public documentation does not prove installed compatibility.

  • Setting up dedicated servers — Public 5.8 tutorial checked; its dedicated-server build route requires a C++ project and source engine build. No target built here.
  • Migrate to Iris — Official 5.8 Migrate to Iris page checked on 2026-10-09: Experimental notice; Iris and Replication Graph cannot be used by the same network driver. No runtime adoption test performed.
  • PostgreSQL transaction isolation — Official current documentation resolved to PostgreSQL 18; transaction isolation and whole-transaction retry requirements checked.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
